entities.summary:
Anthemius was a praetorian prefect of the East in the later reign of Arcadius and the first years of Theodosius II, during which time he led the government of the Eastern Roman Empire on behalf of the child emperor and supervised the construction of the first set of the Theodosian Walls.

As a key figure in the Eastern Roman Empire, Anthemius played a crucial role in the governance of the region, which included the provinces of Asia Minor, Thrace, and Dacia.

His leadership during this period had a lasting impact on the empire's military and administrative structures, and his legacy can be seen in the continued development of the Theodosian Walls, which remained a vital defense system for centuries.

The legacy of Anthemius serves as a testament to the enduring power of Roman governance and the importance of effective leadership in times of crisis.

The construction of the first set of the Theodosian Walls, commissioned during Anthemius' tenure, remains a striking example of the empire's military prowess and engineering capabilities.

The influence of Anthemius' policies and decisions can still be felt in the modern-day borders and governance structures of the region.
